version.changelog: Updated for 2026 with benchmark-backed model selection and clearer guidance for modern image generation stacks.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: image-generation
Version: 1.0.3

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle for AI Image Generation is classified as benign. All code snippets and instructions, including shell commands for setup (`mkdir`, `cp`, `test -f`, `test -n` in `setup.md`, `migration.md`) and Python network calls (`requests`, `openai`, `replicate` in `api-patterns.md`, `gpt-image.md`, `replicate.md`), are directly aligned with the stated purpose of interacting with legitimate image generation APIs or managing local configuration files. The `SKILL.md` transparently declares external endpoints and data sent, and explicitly states it does not store API keys or upload files outside chosen provider requests. There is no evidence of intentional harmful behavior, data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, persistence mechanisms, obfuscation, or malicious prompt injection attempts against the agent.

llm.summary: This skill is a documentation-style image generation helper that clearly discloses its provider API use and limited local preference memory.

dimensions.detail: Optional API keys and external provider calls are proportionate for image generation and are disclosed, including the fact that prompts and optional reference images leave the machine.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no executable installer in the artifact, but provider docs include unpinned pip install examples for Replicate and local Stable Diffusion stacks, which users should run in an isolated environment.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to choosing models, using provider APIs, managing prompts, and avoiding outdated aliases; I found no prompt hijacking, hidden role changes, destructive commands, or unrelated authority.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates or updates local preference memory under ~/image-generation/ and an optional history file; this is disclosed, limited to workflow preferences/project context, and does not store API keys or create background persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently support AI image generation, provider selection, prompt guidance, edits, and local or hosted model workflows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending prompts and any reference images to the selected image provider. Use environment variables for API keys, avoid sensitive or regulated images unless provider policy allows it, and run the optional pip installs in a dedicated virtual environment with pinned dependencies where possible.
llm.findings:
[PE3] unexpected: The cited text only tells users to obtain API keys from provider dashboards or settings and use environment variables; I found no credential-file access or secret harvesting, and setup explicitly says not to ask users to paste secrets into chat.
[E1] expected: Provider API examples send prompts and sometimes reference images to external image-generation services, which is core to the skill's purpose and disclosed in SKILL.md with an endpoint table.
[SQP-2] expected: Privacy-relevant behavior exists, but the top-level artifact discloses that prompts and reference images may leave the machine and identifies the providers; some per-provider pages could repeat that warning more clearly.
[EA2] unexpected: The flagged phrases are cautionary guidance such as checking docs and not requesting secrets, not autonomous high-impact action or removal of user confirmation.
[T08] expected: The unpinned pip install examples are purpose-aligned setup snippets for image-generation tooling, but users should pin versions or use lock files and virtual environments before running them.
